expectations.text: Notes are factored by CONCEPT, not by source (no 'Make It Stick notes' / 'Ahrens notes' section headers)
expectations.evidence: Single doc organized 'by concept, not by source' with concept sections (Desirable difficulties, Retrieval practice, Spacing...); sources appear only as attributions and a trailing Sources appendix.

expectations.text: Retrieval practice note merges Make It Stick + Karpicke 2011 + Dunlosky under one concept with both/all sources cited
expectations.evidence: 'Retrieval practice (the testing effect)' section cites Make It Stick as source, Karpicke & Blunt 2011 as evidence, and 'rated high utility by Dunlosky 2013' as related — all three under one concept.

expectations.text: Note titles are claim-like statements (e.g. 'retrieval practice beats rereading'), not category labels
expectations.evidence: Titles are topic/term labels, not claims: 'Interleaving', 'Elaboration', 'Retrieval practice (the testing effect)', 'Spacing / distributed practice', 'The generation effect' — none states the finding in the title.

expectations.text: Related notes are explicitly linked (wikilinks or equivalent cross-references), incl. generation-effect connection the input flags with 'connects to the karpicke finding?'
expectations.evidence: Sections cross-reference via markdown anchors ('Instances:', 'Related:'), and the generation-effect section keeps 'Open question: connects to the Karpicke finding on [retrieval practice]?'.

expectations.text: Spacing note preserves the Cepeda 'gap scales with retention interval' claim with attribution
expectations.evidence: 'Evidence: Cepeda et al. meta-analysis — the optimal spacing gap scales with the retention interval: "cram for tomorrow, space for forever."'

expectations.text: Storage strength vs retrieval strength (Bjork) is its own concept note
expectations.evidence: Dedicated section 'Storage strength vs. retrieval strength' attributed to Bjork, with the 'different paper? — unverified' caveat preserved.

expectations.text: An index/MOC or linked list exists and is consistent with the skill's ~10-note threshold
expectations.evidence: A 'Map' section at the top links all 11 concept sections by anchor — an index consistent with having 10+ notes.

expectations.text: Ends with a counts line whose numbers reconcile (incl. folded/merged source mentions)
expectations.evidence: Document ends with a Sources appendix; no counts/reconciliation line exists anywhere.
